title: Why automate: human error, scale and repeatability

videos.script: Three routers. One line of configuration each. It sounds like five minutes of work. {{three}} On the first router, the line goes in correctly. On the second, one key is pressed twice, and the router accepts the wrong network without a word. The third router never gets its session, because something else came up. {{mistakes}} Each router looks fine on its own. The problem only shows when you ask all three the same question. {{ask}} This lesson makes the same change with a Python script. It types the line the same way every time, and it saves the configuration every time. Then it learns to ask before changing, so running it twice is safe. {{script}} Then we separate what the network should be from how to get it there. Describe it in a file, check the file, apply it, and read the routers back. {{cycle}} Every lesson after this one strengthens one of those four steps. And every command in them runs on a lab you build first, in this lesson, on your own computer: three routers, a model-driven device, NetBox and a service desk, all inside one Ubuntu machine. {{lab}}
